title: Choose the visual world for Wilber's works
question: Which direction has the strongest shareable infographic idea without sacrificing the history?

options.label: Evolutionary Atlas
options.lineage: nineteenth-century scientific foldouts and phylogenetic plates
options.thesis: Wilber's books become specimens in an evolving field of ideas, arrayed across real publication time.
options.viewport: A landscape foldout: forty works run left to right from 1977 to 2024, five soft phase strata pass behind them, and a few key books enlarge into annotated specimens whose conceptual descendants branch forward.
options.risk: The scientific authority can overstate certainty unless inferred links and fuzzy phase boundaries remain visibly provisional.

raised.raise: Confidence lives in line character: documented descent is solid, editorial inference is a faint ghost track.
All forty works remain findable at overview scale instead of becoming decorative background.

options.label: The Exhibition Wall
options.lineage: museum chronology walls and landmark exhibition graphics
options.thesis: The complete body of work reads as one monumental exhibition wall with a strong editorial rhythm.
options.viewport: A panoramic 1977–2024 wall: every cover sits on the chronological baseline, key works break scale, and five large phase captions explain the intellectual turns in a sentence each.
options.risk: It is the most immediately legible direction and therefore the most familiar; the editorial composition must be exceptional to feel ownable.

options.label: Thought Woven
options.lineage: Jacquard diagrams, woven brocade, and punched instruction cards
options.thesis: Five intellectual threads cross, separate, and recombine until the books resolve into a single woven pattern.
options.viewport: A dark horizontal tapestry: time is the warp, themes are the weft, books are woven labels, and the mature synthesis appears where the threads become densest around 1995–2006.
options.case: It creates the strongest visual metaphor and a beautiful screenshot, while chronology and forty labels remain possible in a disciplined border ledger.
options.risk: The metaphor can outrun the content, especially when edition relationships need precise labels rather than poetic threads.

options.label: Forty Works, One Field
options.lineage: dense cultural catalogs and annotated field guides
options.thesis: All forty works become a single collectible field: tiny, numbered, and impossible not to scan.
options.viewport: A poster-like chronological grid of all forty works, grouped by decade with phase bands cutting across it; red pencil routes circle the essential books and connect documented reworkings.
options.case: It best solves the simple all-books artifact and invites zooming, counting, and sharing, but carries less intellectual drama than the atlas.
options.risk: At social-feed size it may read as texture before it reads as Wilber unless the title and phase arc dominate.

options.label: Kosmic Event Display
options.thesis: Books radiate from successive theoretical breakthroughs like tracks from collisions.
options.viewport: Five conceptual events emit book tracks through concentric decades.
options.case: Visually arresting, but concentric time obscures the chronological catalog and over-dramatizes a few turning points.
options.risk: It can resemble a science-fiction dashboard more than intellectual history.
options.kept: Use line weight and opacity to encode evidential confidence.

canonCard.label: The polished timeline
canonCard.thesis: A clean horizontal timeline with phase bands, cover thumbnails, filters, and detail panels.
canonCard.viewport: A responsive 1977–2024 axis with forty covers and a simple phase legend.
canonCard.risk: Clear and useful, but unlikely to become an image people remember independently of the site.
